correctness.rationale: Exact algebra gives D4^2=||(A-B)(A+B)||_2^2. On trace-2t two-by-two Hermitian matrices the Pauli expansion yields 2||x-y||^2(4t^2+||x+y||^2). For each triple the affine plane can be written w+V with w orthogonal to V, and the pairwise values are Euclidean squared chord lengths for the single map zeta->(sqrt(4t^2+4||w||^2) zeta,zeta^2), up to the factor sqrt(2). This proves a universal metric, including boundary rank-deficient matrices and trace t>0. Exact integer products give full-cone D4 squared values (240,201,1) and strict inequality 361>201. Dimension one equals |a^2-b^2|. Checker arithmetic is corroboration only.

value.rationale: The recent general p-Bures distance is proved metric only for p<=2. The new result pinpoints a natural positive slice beyond that range: every fixed-trace qubit cone is still metric at the first even super-Hilbert exponent p=4, while changing trace destroys the triangle inequality already in the minimal nontrivial dimension. The exact three-point Euclidean realization is a structural explanation, not an isolated finite computation. The paired positive and negative results give a meaningful minimal-dimensional boundary for matrix affinity metrics.
